recipes.name: Lemony Chicken with Artichoke Hearts
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Combine the flour and salt on a plate, then gently press the chicken breasts into the flour mixture to coat. Shake off the excess flour. Arrange the chicken in the skillet and cook until browned on each side, about 10 minutes. Add the lemon juice, chicken broth, Worcestershire sauce, vermouth, garlic, bay leaf, and basil. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes. Stir in the artichoke hearts, and continue simmering until the chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 15 minutes more.
Mix the cornstarch and water in a small bowl. Stir the mixture into the chicken, and continue cooking until thickened, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemony Chicken with Artichoke Hearts
raw_recipe.description: This dish of tender chicken breasts simmered in a light lemon sauce makes the perfect weeknight dinner. Serve it with your favorite pasta and a side salad for a complete meal.

review.reviewBody: I usually try my best to follow the recipe the first time around. I don't like to make any changes, but sometimes it gets a bit pricey to buy new ingredients you have never used before. I have never heard of the item vermouth. I looked up on the internet to see what it was and what would be a possibly good substitute for it. I used Sherry instead. I also used only half of what the recipe recommended for lemon juice since it looked like a lot when I was squeezing it into the skillet. I halved the recipe since I was just cooking for myself. Overall, the dish was very tasty and I would definitely make it again. It's a great dish! Also there is no photo?! I uploaded one of mine. :)

We are doing WW; sautéed breast cutlets in a little butter and olive oil. Later added the Lemon juice, Worchester, Vermouth, chopped fresh garlic, chicken broth, basil and bay leaf. After a simmer added artichokes, can of mushrooms, can of white beans...simmered and then added 8 oz. of fresh baby spinach. Thickened a little bit with Wegmans Pan searing flour and 2 tablespoons of pasta sauce. Delicious. Low carbs.

I halved the recipe since I was only cooking for one, and I used chicken tenders instead of breast halves and white wine in place of the vermouth. Because the tenders would cook much more quickly than breasts, I just browned the tenders and kept them warm while I made the sauce, then added the tenders at the end for about 10 minutes. The chicken turned out moist and tender, but I did not care for the sauce. I found it too lemony and also the Worcestershire sauce was too pronounced for my taste. Also, after I added the cornstarch mixture, the sauce became too thick so I thinned it with more chicken broth. I used 1 lemon since I was making a half recipe, but perhaps the lemon juice should be measured in teaspoons or tablespoons. Next time I'll reduce the lemon juice substantially and omit the Worcestershire sauce. Sliced sauteed mushrooms would be a nice addition, I think.
By: Mary

I used chicken tenders instead of chicken breast halves. Since they were fully cooked after browning in the pan, I removed them to make the sauce so they didn't dry out, then returned them to the pan after the sauce had thickened. I also added 1/2 a diced onion as the sauce cooked down, as one of the comments recommended. I also sub'd white wine for the vermouth. Served it with steamed green beans. The whole family really enjoyed it - even the toddler people. Great healthy dish.

This was awesome!!! The only change I made was to use white wine for the vermouth and I used cutlets so I cut down the simmering time to 10 minutes then took chicken out of the pan to mix in the artichoke and thicken with the cornstarch. I love lemon so it was just right for me, I only had one lemon so I used the zest also. I'm on dialysis and have to watch my salt intake and this was a wonderful...healthy and tasty. Will definitely makes this again!!!

I have made this several times now and we really like it! I only use the juice of one lemon (just my personal taste). I am not big fan of white meat so I cut off the tenderloin, filet the breast, and then pound them thin with a meat mallet. The chicken is fork tender cooked this way! It is wonderful served over Jasmine rice or angel hair pasta. Thank you for the wonderful recipe!

This is great! I added crimini (baby Bella) mushroom slices the last 10-15 mins and capers the last 5 mins. I love artichoke hearts so used TWO cans. Used Gewürztraminer wine as that's what was handy- very good! Used both lemons. I can't think of anything it "needs"- had excellent flavor! Also, I'm a celiac so I used a gluten free all purpose flour for coating the chicken. I could probably do without the worcestershire sauce, only because I don't really like it, but that's not a fault of the recipe, just a personal preference.

Instead of dredging in flour, used crushed croutons. Didn't have vermouth, so substituted white cooking wine. Didn't have worcestershire, so substituted soy sauce with a touch of brown sugar. Added peas and carrots, and served it over a quinoa/rice mixture. Great! Will definitely be making it again!

Light, healthy and easy. Kids did not care for it but the adults enjoyed it. Served over pasta. Did not use flour. Instead chopped chicken into bite size and cooked with olive oil until no longer pink. Added celery salt and dash of tarragon to add more flavor. Also used white wine and lemon pepper spice. Did not have lemons so used 3 small limes.

I made a couple of changes based on experiences with similar recipes - I sliced the chicken instead of leaving it whole, and browned it without any breading (breading will just get soggy in the sauce). I served it over whole grain spaghetti and it was pretty good. I think it would be better with more sauce; I'll make it again and double the sauce ingredients.

This was a very nice change of pace dish for us. I wanted to prepare something light, lemony, and springy, and this fit the bill. I used good sized chicken tenders, and pounded them flat, which decreased the cooking time. I added some pepper and oregano to the four, and a touch of olive oil to less butter to saute. I made the sauce as published, but did decrease the lemon to one, as my lemon was good sized and figured I could add more if needed. This doesn't make a ton of sauce, next time I would double or triple as it is delicious and great over the angel hair. I think I'll add capers next time too for a touch of color and bite. Maybe some fresh parsley, too. Thanks for sharing your recipe with us Gurtrug, I enjoyed preparing it.
I love this recipe! We enjoy it over angel hair pasta. I do add a tablesppon of capers and some parm on top.

I loved it, I actually used both lemons because I love lemon but you can adjust any of the seasonings or flavors to accommodate to your taste buds. We used thighs and added Dijon with chardonnay to the cornstarch and it really added to the wow factor.

I saw some people said this recipe was too lemony and/or too salty. So, I only used one lemon, non-marinated artichokes, and skipped adding any salt. Other than that, I followed the recipe as written and it was perfect. Just lemony enough and the chicken came out moist and delicious. My husband and son loved it. It was also quick and very easy. I will be making this again.
Very good. I be made this before but forgot to rate. 2 lemons is way to much, I would start with a half and work my way up. I did add capers to the dish as well. Thank you for sharing.
Very similar to how I make Chicken Piccata. I served it over rice but linguine will do just as well.
This recipe was ok. The chicken was very tender, and the recipe was easy to prepare. I didn’t have vermouth so I substituted white wine; so, I’ll try again and see if the overall flavor is better.
Easy to make, very tasty. Making it again a week later!
Very sour! Too much Worcestershire, not enough corn starch.
Wow this is lemony! I think adding water chestnuts or mushrooms would help soften the punch. My husband and I liked it but not my 9yr old. Not sure I'll make it again.
